entries.title: Genesis 35:2
segments: Change your garments; a symbol of the inward purification of the soul.

entries.title: Genesis 35:3
segments: When God has graciously appeared for us in trouble, answered our prayers, and visited us in mercy, we should hasten to acknowledge his goodness, and render the praise and thanksgiving which are his due and our reasonable service.

entries.title: Genesis 35:4
segments: Ear-rings; probably graven with superstitious devices, and used as amulets or charms.

entries.title: Genesis 35:8
segments:
Allon-bachuth; the oak of weeping. 
 
Domestics who perform with fidelity their appropriate duties to God and to men, add greatly to the comfort and usefulness of families, and are justly entitled to confidence, affection, and respect.  By the wise and the good they will be greatly beloved while they live, and deeply lamented when they die.

entries.title: Genesis 35:14
segments: Whenever God especially blesses men, pious gratitude should lead them publicly to acknowledge and adore him.

entries.title: Genesis 35:16
segments: Ephrath; also called Bethlehem, about six miles south of Jerusalem.

entries.title: Genesis 35:18
segments:
Ben-oni; son of my sorrow. 
 
  Benjamin; meaning, son of the right hand.

entries.title: Genesis 35:19
segments: Not a thought, word, or action escapes the notice of God, or ever passes from his remembrance.  Give me children, said Rachel, or else I die.
God gave her children, and she died.  More wise, more safe, more blessed is it to say, Not my will, but thine be done.

entries.title: Genesis 35:20
segments: Unto this day; the time when Moses wrote this history.

entries.title: Genesis 35:21
segments: Tower of Edar; that is tower of the flock.
It is supposed to have been not far from Bethlehem.

entries.title: Genesis 35:29
segments: The death of a parent should ever awaken new affection and kindness in children; and while they unite in paying respect to his memory, they should be grateful for his virtues, and so far as he obeyed God, imitate his example.
